notes: With skill 94% vs 81% without (+13 pts, 1 run each, 12 evals); 42% fewer tokens (45.6k vs 78.5k) and ~13% faster. Baselines had to page all 133 rows because MCP query_records ignores search.
Non-discriminating on pass rate: evals 01, 03, 04, 11 pass 100% in both configs; there the skill's value is cost (1-2 HTTP calls vs full-table dumps), not correctness.

Environment, not skill: in evals 07 and 12 (and partly 05, 06, 08) Claude Code's auto-mode permission classifier blocked kb.py dry runs (and once a read) in subagents, so preview assertions failed or were satisfied by equivalent checks. Allowlisting kb.py read and dry-run commands would remove this.

Skill gap (eval 02): find matches substrings, so the plural 'labels' missed 'K3S - Create new service' (which has 'label'); the baseline found it and gave the better answer. Fix: also match the singular form of plural terms.
Skill gap (eval 09): for-work/refer need a record id; the run had to look the project id up with a separate REST call. Fix: accept project:"<title>".
Skill gap (eval 11): the baseline audit found password reuse across entries, plaintext private keys and a bare password-only body that doctor G missed; doctor covers structure, not content quality.

Baseline risks the skill prevents: eval 10 baseline would archive without asking and its reference check could not see one-way refer_knowledge links; eval 08 and 09 baselines overwrite whole fields instead of appending.
